images.title: Moving the point left
images.purpose: Show the rule for dividing by 10, 100 or 1000: the decimal point moves left once for each zero in the divisor.
images.composition: Two short rows of working are stacked in the centre, each with curved hop arrows above the digits; plenty of white space at the sides.
exact_structure: Row 1 (upper): the text "123 ÷ 10 = 12.3" in large dark text #1F2937; above the answer 12.3, exactly 1 curved teal #0072B2 hop arrow pointing left, starting just right of the digit 3 and landing on the decimal point between 2 and 3, so it passes over exactly 1 digit.
Beside row 1, on the right, a small teal #0072B2 tag reading "1 zero, 1 place".

Row 2 (lower): the text "12 ÷ 1000 = 0.012" in large dark text #1F2937; above the answer 0.012, exactly 3 curved amber #E69F00 hop arrows in a chain pointing left, starting just right of the final 2 and landing on the decimal point, each arrow passing over exactly 1 of the digits 2, 1 and 0.
In 0.012, the 0 written just after the decimal point is coloured reddish purple #CC79A7 to show the zero written in front because the digits ran out.
Beside row 2, on the right, a small amber #E69F00 tag reading "3 zeroes, 3 places".
No other rows, no place value chart, no fractions.
rejection: the number of hop arrows in a row differing from 1 in row 1 or 3 in row 2
arrows pointing to the right instead of the left
the zero after the point in 0.012 missing
images.takeaway: Dividing by 10, 100 or 1000 moves the point left 1, 2 or 3 places, writing zeroes in front if needed.
images.description: Two rows: 123 ÷ 10 = 12.3 with one hop arrow to the left, and 12 ÷ 1000 = 0.012 with three hop arrows to the left and a highlighted zero.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text on the rule for dividing by 10, 100 and 1000.
images.teaching_notes: Count the zeroes in the divisor, then count the hop arrows; the two counts always match.

image_decisions.why: The rule is about movement of the point, which a picture with hop arrows shows far better than words.
